maria_ml: Heads up — ran a HF->Redwood conversion for the new spm model and our chat templates started emitting weird joiner artifacts. Seeing outputs like `Hello\u2060world` (U+2060) and occasional `Hello\u200Bworld` (ZWSP).

sam_engineer: Yikes. Is that from the tokenizer or from our config.json remap? Any quick repro? :thinking_face:

maria_ml: Minimal repro below. Tokenizer built with SentencePiece (fast HF tokenizer). After conversion to BPE-backed tokenizer we get token ids that include a joiner token glued to the following word.
```
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('local/spm-model', use_fast=True)
print(tok.tokenize('Hello world'))
# -> ['Hello', '\u2060world']
```

jin_research: Looks like the spm model used U+2581 (▁) as space marker originally. During conversion we attempted to replace that with a joiner char to mimic BPE behavior, but the mapping script accidentally used a zero-width joiner for some merges. Also saw special_tokens_map entries for `<pad>` vs `pad_token` that shifted indices.

sam_engineer: Do we have failing tests? opsbot, did the nightly eval catch this?

opsbot: nightly-qa:quantization -> 1 failing sample (diff against baseline). Failure reason: token-level mismatch in chat template rendering. Trace attached in CI log.

maria_ml: Root cause appears to be twofold: 1) the conversion script inserts an explicit joiner character (U+2060) into the vocab for some merges, 2) our chat-template rendering strips whitespace then rejoins tokens, which collapses the visible space and leaves the joiner.

jin_research: Quick mitigation options:
- re-run conversion ensuring we map SentencePiece '▁' -> leading-space prefix (no invisible joiner)
- sanitize vocab after conversion: remove U+200B/U+2060 entries and remap affected ids to correct tokens
- in the console/renderer, normalize outputs with NFKC and replace zero-widths: `re.sub('[\u200B\u2060]', '', s)`

sam_engineer: Can we patch the conversion script? I vaguely remember a `replace_extra_whitespace` flag in our adapter.

maria_ml: Yep. I pushed a quick fix to the converter to prefer explicit visible space marker and to verify special_tokens indices. Repro commands I used:
```
# conversion (local)
python tools/hf_spm_to_bpe.py --input model --out converted --sanitize-joiners
python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; print(AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('converted').tokenize('Hello world'))"
```

jin_research: After sanitize-joiners flag it tokenizes correctly?

maria_ml: Yes in my env. Also updated our CI to run a small tokenization roundtrip: join->tokenize->detokenize and check for invisible codepoints. Added a unit test to catch U+200B/U+2060 in outputs.

sam_engineer: Nice. Any downstream perf or quantization impacts?

maria_ml: Quant runs look fine — the issue was purely a text-level artifact. But important: if special_tokens indices shift, quantized kernels that rely on pad/sep ids can break, so I verified pad/sep mapping after conversion.

jin_research: Filed a follow-up: please add a short comment in the converter explaining why we sanitize joiners and a link to this thread. I'll add a tiny eval comparing BLEU/ROUGE on a few chattemplates to ensure no semantic regressions.

maria_ml: TLDR: spm->bpe conversion can accidentally introduce invisible joiner chars. Fix: sanitize vocab, validate special_token ids, add roundtrip test to CI. Thanks for the quick triage :+1:
